audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL transaction lifecycle (EIP-658 receipts, EIP-1559 fee market, EIP-155 replay protection, bloom filters, EIP-2566 RPC), CL fork choice (safe block), CL fork transitions (Fulu), CL/EL P2P networking (EIP-6800, EIP-7892), and CL light client operations (Deneb).

EL.threat: Submit malformed transactions, exploit fee calculation edge cases, ABI spoofing via EIP-2566, replay attacks across chains
Eclipse attacks, send invalid blocks with incorrect base fees or receipt status codes

CL.threat: Propose blocks with invalid fork versions, manipulate safe block determination, submit conflicting attestations
Advertise incompatible fork digests, eclipse attacks during fork transitions (Fulu, BPO forks), serve manipulated light client headers

misclassified_entities.reason: The 'Transaction Executor' in the bloom filter spec is the EVM execution engine, which is an internal EL component, not an external entity. Log data originates from smart contract execution within the EL.

Labeled as 'Engine API Consumer (Execution Layer)' in the safe block spec. The EL is an in-scope target component, not an external entity per se. However, from the CL's perspective the EL queries the CL for the safe block hash via Engine API, so this is better modeled as the EL querying the CL — the CL is the provider. Re-modeled below as CL providing data to EL via Engine API.

The 'Replay Attacker' in EIP-155 is a threat actor model, not a distinct external entity with its own entry point. Replay attacks come through the same P2P/RPC channels as normal transactions. Covered by EXT-TX-BROADCASTER-P2P.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated public RPC interface. Users submit EIP-1559 type-2 transactions and EIP-155 signed transactions. No authentication required. All transaction data is potentially malformed or malicious.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via JSON-RPC (EIP-2566)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApp provides ABI metadata alongside transaction data. ABI is untrusted and may be spoofed to mislead wallet users. Function selector collision attacks are possible.

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Client via JSON-RPC (queries)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External clients querying receipts (EIP-658 status codes) and logs (bloom filter lookups). Unauthenticated read path. Query parameters could be crafted to cause resource exhaustion.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet/Signer via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External wallet software that signs transactions with EIP-155 chain ID protection. The signed transaction data entering the EL is untrusted and requires full validation including chain ID verification and signature recovery.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Broadcaster via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote peers broadcasting signed transactions over the P2P network. Includes potential replay attack vectors (EIP-155). All received transactions require full validation: signature, chain ID, nonce, balance, fee checks.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Validator) via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators producing blocks with EIP-1559 base fees, gas limits, and transaction receipts (EIP-658). All block-level fields must be independently validated: base fee calculation, gas limit bounds, gas used, receipt status codes.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: CL communicates safe block hash (from justified checkpoint) and new payloads to EL via JWT-authenticated Engine API. Channel is authenticated, but payload content (block data, safe block hash) must still be validated. Incorrect safe block hash could mislead EL clients.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: EL provides execution payload validation results back to CL. JWT-authenticated channel. CL uses EL validation status to make fork choice decisions. Incorrect validation results could compromise consensus.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via CL P2P (gossipsub)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote CL peers communicating via gossipsub with fork-digest-scoped topics. Relevant for EIP-6800 (Verkle fork version), EIP-7892 (BPO fork digest rotation), and Fulu fork transitions. Peers may advertise incompatible fork digests, attempt eclipse attacks during fork transitions, or send invalid messages.

trusted_external_entities.name: Light Client Peer via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Light clients requesting Deneb-format headers with blob gas fields from full nodes. From the full node perspective, light client requests are untrusted and could be used for resource exhaustion.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: EIP-1559 fee fields (max_fee_per_gas >= base_fee), balance check (gas_limit * max_fee + value), EIP-155 chain ID verification, signature recovery, nonce check.
Query parameters must be validated. Bloom filter pre-filtering reduces I/O but false positives require full log verification. Rate limiting recommended to prevent resource exhaustion.
ABI-to-data function selector validation is mandatory. Selector match does NOT guarantee ABI accuracy (4-byte collision possible). Wallet must clearly indicate ABI source is untrusted DApp.
EIP-155 chain ID must be extracted from v parameter and verified against network CHAIN_ID. Legacy v=27/28 transactions accepted for backward compatibility but lack cross-chain replay protection.

All P2P-received transactions require identical validation as RPC-submitted transactions. Additionally, replay attack detection via EIP-155 chain ID check. Transactions with mismatched chain IDs must be rejected.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: devp2p block gossip / Engine API newPayload
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block validation must verify: EIP-1559 base fee matches calculation from parent, gas limit within ±1/1024 of parent, gas_used <= gas_limit, minimum gas limit >= 5000, all receipt status codes (EIP-658) correctly reflect execution outcomes.

JWT authentication validates channel identity. EL must independently validate all payload content: block structure, state transitions, receipt generation. Safe block hash from CL (justified checkpoint) must be used only as advisory — EL should not assume safe block is finalized.
JWT authentication validates channel identity. CL must handle invalid/syncing responses gracefully. Incorrect VALID status for an invalid payload could cause CL to build on an invalid chain.

Fork digest verification required at connection time. During fork transitions (Fulu, EIP-6800, EIP-7892 BPO forks), peers with mismatched fork digests must be disconnected. ENR nfd field must be validated. All gossip messages require full consensus validation regardless of peer identity.

Light client requests must be rate-limited. Deneb-format headers must include blob_gas_used and excess_blob_gas only for blocks at or after DENEB_FORK_EPOCH. Pre-Deneb blocks must use legacy header format.
